idiom_name: test-local type implementing the small interface, handed to the SUT (func adapter for one-method interfaces)
implementation_notes: Go interfaces are satisfied implicitly and are conventionally one or two methods, so the idiomatic shunt is a struct declared in the _test.go file that implements the interface and is passed to the SUT; because a Go test is a function rather than an object, that test-local value is the self, and the whole double fits in a few lines beside the test. Where the collaborator is a one-method interface, the standard library's own adapter pattern applies -- a function type with a method (http.HandlerFunc) or a struct with a func field lets the test pass a closure, which is an Inner Test Double rather than a Self Shunt. Hand-written doubles remain the baseline for recording; generated or testify mocks enter only when cardinality, argument matching or ordering must be verified.
pitfalls: Package-level recording state is shared by every test in the package; keep the shunt struct local to the test function so parallel tests (t.Parallel) cannot race on it.
A SUT that calls back from another goroutine turns the recording slice into a data race under -race; guard it with a mutex or record through a channel if the collaborator is concurrent.
Embedding an interface in the shunt to avoid implementing unused methods makes unexpected calls panic with a nil dereference instead of failing an assertion meaningfully.
